hypothesis_or_artifact: REGISTRATION Sections 17.3 and 15.6, the weight-concentration explanation of the BLOCKED verdict
label: DERIVED
claim_quote:
The value-weighted book holds a mean of **71.9 names and behaves like 29.7
effective names**, because the heaviest name carries **14.9 percent** of the book
and the heaviest five carry **33.8 percent**.
evidence_summary: The two figures are computed on two different books. 71.909 is MembershipSeries.mean_width() (portfolio/membership.py:46-54), written to portfolio.json at portfolio/build.py:59; it averages len(book) over non-empty sessions BEFORE the not_priced drop. 29.731282, 0.149323 and 0.337911 are computed at portfolio/returns.py:213-217 on 'priced', the book AFTER that drop (priced = [n for n in book if n in members], returns.py:189-190), the same drop that removes 13,750 name-sessions. The book that actually produced 29.7, the weight shares and the 49.35 has a mean width of 66.93: power.json series[0] book_width_mean 66.93, whose source is widths.append(len(priced)) at returns.py:210. Recomputed from the dispersion store's own book_width column: 66.92522278186749 over n = 2,581 sessions. Effect: the document's ratio is 71.909/29.731 = 2.42x; the like-for-like ratio on the book that produced both numbers is 66.925/29.731 = 2.25x, so the error makes the concentration look worse than it is and therefore favours the BLOCKED explanation. The verdict itself is untouched - the MDE reproduces exactly. The same pairing appears at REGISTRATION.md:749 ('| 126, value-weighted | 71.9 | 29.7 |' under a column headed 'Names held') and at progress.md:31-32 and :249-250. The 14.9% and 33.8% shares themselves verify (0.149323, 0.337911).
recomputation: Inputs: var/insider_dispersion.db centered_excess.book_width for (hold_sessions 126, weighting value_weighted), n = 2,581; and the membership series rebuilt from var/insider_corpus.db.event crossed with var/insider_market.db.session. Method: arithmetic mean of each width series. Results: 66.92522278186749 (priced) and 71.90895121014215 (pre-drop, which reproduces corpus.json mean_book_width exactly). Tolerance 1e-9.
would_resolve: Stating the priced width beside the membership width - 'holds a mean of 71.9 names of which 66.9 are priced on an average session, and behaves like 29.7 effective names' - or labelling the Section 15.6 column 'Names in the book before the mid-hold universe drop'.
confidence_why: Both figures are recomputed from stored primitives and the two code paths that produce them are three lines apart in the same function.
disclosure_ref: ADR-009 (InsiderExperiment/DECISIONS.md:258-280) discloses the mid-hold drop and its 13,750 name-sessions, and Section 15.1 correctly labels 71.9 as the corpus-side mean book width, but nothing states that the width and the effective-names figure are computed on different books, and Section 17.3 presents them as one sentence about one book.

hypothesis_or_artifact: REGISTRATION Section 17.4 and ADR-011, the equal-weighted secondary
label: DERIVED
claim_quote:
On the identical names, the equal-weighted book holds **71.9 and behaves like
66.9**, with tracking error of **6.86 percent** and an MDE of **34.29 bp per
month, which would have fired DEGRADED**.
evidence_summary: The 6.86%, the 34.29 and the DEGRADED branch all verify exactly (recomputed TE 6.8556% and MDE 34.2897; 20 < 34.2897 <= 40 at section0.py:62). This finding concerns only the '71.9 and behaves like 66.9' pair. For an equal-weighted book the inverse Herfindahl IS the name count by construction: _effective_names at portfolio/returns.py:118-124 with raw = np.ones(len(names)) at returns.py:101, so the effective-names figure for the EW series can only equal the mean PRICED width. It does, to six decimals: portfolio.json[3].diagnostics.book_effective_names = 66.925223, and the mean of book_width for (126, equal_weighted) in var/insider_dispersion.db is 66.92522278186749 over n = 2,581; power.json series[3] carries book_width_mean 66.93 for the same series. The equal-weighted book therefore holds 66.93 names and behaves like 66.93 names; the stated '71.9 -> 66.9' implies a ~7% concentration effect inside an equal-weighted book, which cannot exist. Asserted more strongly at REGISTRATION.md:863 ('Both books hold 71.9 names.') and at progress.md:42 and :252-253. The membership half of the claim is true: both 126-session rows of portfolio.json carry book_width_mean 71.909 and identical dropped maps, so the two books do hold the same names; it is the pairing of that width with the effective-names figure that is not. The true figures make the secondary's book LESS collapsed, not more.
recomputation: Inputs: var/insider_dispersion.db centered_excess.book_width for (126, equal_weighted), n = 2,581, against reports/stage_a1/portfolio.json[3].diagnostics.book_effective_names. Method: arithmetic mean of the stored width series compared with the stored diagnostic. Result: 66.92522278186749 against 66.925223 - they agree, which is forced by the equal-weight construction. Tolerance 1e-6.
would_resolve: Restating as 'the equal-weighted book prices 66.9 names on an average session and behaves like all 66.9 of them, against the value-weighted book's 29.7', which is a sharper statement of the same point.
confidence_why: The identity is forced by the code (equal weights make inverse Herfindahl equal the name count) and is confirmed numerically to six decimals.

hypothesis_or_artifact: The session-cost record ('cost, measured rather than asserted') and the ETA-against-actual table
label: DERIVED
claim_quote:
**Cost, measured rather than asserted.** The commit record puts Stage A.1 at
about 51 minutes of session wall clock, 18:20 to 19:11, and Stage Z.1 at about
20 minutes. The Z.1 brief records five hours. The commit record cannot confirm
that figure, which presumably counts operator time between stages that this
repository does not observe.
evidence_summary: Two independent failures in the same passage. (1) The eight 'Actual' entries in the table at progress.md:198-205 read 5, 10, 4, 4, 14, 20, 32 and 22 minutes and sum to 111 minutes against the 51 claimed for the same stage (n = 8 task rows); the table's own header at progress.md:193-194 asserts that the actuals are wall clock with boundaries taken from commit timestamps, i.e. that they partition the same interval. The commit record (n = 7 commits, re-read 2026-09-04T18:45Z) is fbfc74e 18:34:56, 398755b 18:38:50, ccc9b13 18:47:16, cb17046 19:11:45, 672b343 19:11:45, d8b81f1 19:11:55, 12d9fd3 23:24:15, all -07:00; 18:20 to 19:11:55 is 51.9 minutes. Three of the eight actuals cannot come from commit boundaries: tasks 5, 6 and 7 claim 20+32+22 = 74 minutes but sit across cb17046/672b343 (identical timestamp, delta 0 s) and d8b81f1 (delta 10 s), while the whole ccc9b13 -> d8b81f1 interval is 24 min 39 s; task 4's 14 min also exceeds its 8 min 26 s commit interval. (2) Exactly one commit belongs to Stage Z.1 (12d9fd3, 23:24:15), and a single commit has no interior interval, so the commit record supplies no Z.1 duration at all - it can put Z.1 at 'about 20 minutes' no more than it can confirm five hours. The only interval the record carries across the boundary is d8b81f1 19:11:55 -> 12d9fd3 23:24:15 = 4 h 12 min 20 s, which is not inconsistent with the brief's five hours. No artifact narrows it: every mtime under reports/, var/ and ledgers/ is <= 2026-08-25 19:10:28 -07:00 (mutations.json; last ledger append 19:06:24), which is the same fact that makes the 'Z.1 changed no result' claim SUPPORTED. The 51-minute figure is itself only partly from the record: its 18:20 start precedes both the first commit (18:34:56) and the first ledger record (18:35:18) and comes from progress.md:193.
recomputation: Inputs: the eight Actual cells at progress.md:198-205 and the seven commit author dates from git log --format='%h %ad' --date=iso-strict. Method: sum the Actual column; difference consecutive commit times; count the commits belonging to Stage Z.1. Results: 111 min against 51.9 min of wall clock; 74 min of claimed task time across a 24 min 39 s commit interval; one Z.1 commit and a 4 h 12 min 20 s gap from the last A.1 commit. Tolerance: +/-1 s on the commit arithmetic, +/-1 min on the column.
would_resolve: Marking the per-task actuals as estimates rather than commit-derived and reconciling the column to the 51.9-minute interval it says it partitions; and attributing the 20 minutes to its actual source (a session clock or the Z.1 brief) rather than to 'the commit record', or stating plainly that the record bounds neither figure and that the only observable is the 4 h 12 min gap.
confidence_why: Both sides are direct reads - one from the document, one from git objects - and the inference that a single commit yields no interval is arithmetic.
invalidation_note: Closed repository; a later commit could only add Z.1 boundaries that did not exist when the sentence was written.
disclosure_ref: The same passage discloses the other half: 'The commit record cannot confirm that figure' of the five-hour brief figure (InsiderExperiment/progress.md:117-118), closing 'Both are recorded rather than one being picked' (progress.md:119). What is not disclosed is that the 20-minute figure is equally unsupported by the record it is attributed to, nor that the document's own ETA table contradicts its own 51-minute figure by more than a factor of two.
